topic: Versioned file-revert operation contracts versus whole-turn or conversation rewind
research_questions: What contracts make a versioned file-revert operation safe, previewable, atomic, auditable, and distinguishable from whole-turn or conversation rewind?
How do Git, IDE, and agent coding systems bind identity, snapshots, workspace state, and rollback scope?
Which race, partial-write, stale-base, conflict, and recovery failure modes require explicit handling?
Which patterns should Puppet Master adopt or reject for file-level versus turn-level recovery?

sources.title: git-restore Documentation
sources.material_relevance: Defines path-scoped restore from a selected tree and separately targets the working tree, index, or both; also documents interactive hunks, deletions, pathspecs, and submodule behavior.

sources.title: git-apply Documentation
sources.material_relevance: Documents dry-run applicability checks, index/worktree coupling, blob-identity-aware three-way application, and conflict outcomes for patch-based change or revert.

sources.title: api-lockfile Documentation
sources.material_relevance: Specifies exclusive lock creation, write-then-rename commit, cleanup on failure, and the old-or-new visibility guarantee that avoids torn reads.

sources.title: git-reflog Documentation
sources.material_relevance: Defines local reference logs for branch and HEAD movement, supplying recoverable reference identity but not a general file-content transaction journal.

sources.title: git-worktree Documentation
sources.material_relevance: Documents multiple linked worktrees, per-worktree HEAD and index state, detached experimental worktrees, locking, pruning, and repair.

sources.title: git-stash Documentation
sources.material_relevance: Shows that working-directory and index snapshots can be represented as commits, scoped by path, inspected, reapplied, and retained when pop encounters conflicts.

sources.title: RFC 5789: PATCH Method for HTTP
sources.material_relevance: Provides a normative partial-update contract: conditional known-base requests, all-or-none application, no partial representation visibility, and conflict/precondition error handling.

sources.title: RFC 6902: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Patch
sources.material_relevance: Defines ordered patch operations, the test guard, failure termination, and the requirement that an unsuccessful patch not be treated as successfully applied.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.material_relevance: Defines strong If-Match validation before state-changing methods, the lost-update protection purpose, and 412 handling for a failed precondition.

sources.title: Review AI-generated code edits
sources.material_relevance: Documents agent-edit review at file, individual-change, and all-files granularity, pending-edit identity, discard/keep actions, sensitive-file approval, and pre-commit review.

sources.title: Revert changes with checkpoints and editing requests
sources.material_relevance: Separates per-edit review from request checkpoints, snapshots affected files before a chat request, restores all later file changes, supports redo, and can show per-request file change counts.

sources.title: User interface
sources.material_relevance: Documents file Timeline and local history entries containing full saved file contents, compare/restore actions, deletion recovery, and bounded size, count, exclusion, and merge-window settings.

findings.claim: Git models file revert as an explicit path-scoped operation whose source and destination layers are named: a selected tree can restore the working tree, the index, or both, and interactive hunks can narrow the change.
findings.notes: The documented pathspec and --staged/--worktree controls make the affected scope materially different from a whole-turn rollback.

findings.claim: Git supplies a preview and compatibility gate for patch application: --check detects whether a patch applies, --index checks both index and worktree consistency, and --3way uses recorded blob identity when available.
findings.notes: A safe revert can therefore separate plan/preview from mutation and can surface a conflict instead of silently overwriting a changed base.

findings.claim: Git's lockfile contract prevents torn file publication by exclusively creating a sidecar lock, writing the new contents there, and atomically renaming it into place; readers are not blocked but see old or new contents when the filesystem rename is atomic.
findings.notes: The same contract also distinguishes writer mutual exclusion from reader consistency, which should be explicit in an operation contract.

findings.claim: Git reflogs record updates to local references and HEAD movement, while stash entries provide commit-backed working-directory and index snapshots that can be inspected and reapplied.
findings.notes: Reference history and working-state snapshots are separate recovery surfaces; neither should be conflated with conversation history.

findings.claim: Git worktrees bind checkout context to a distinct worktree with its own HEAD and index while sharing repository objects, and support lock, prune, and repair operations for lifecycle control.
findings.notes: This is an isolation pattern for agent attempts or previews, not a request-level rewind mechanism.

findings.claim: The PATCH standard requires the entire change set to apply atomically, prohibits exposing a partially modified representation, and recommends conditional requests when a patch depends on a known base.
findings.notes: RFC 5789 explicitly covers multiple directly affected files and identifies 409 or 412 classes for conflicting state or failed preconditions.

findings.claim: JSON Patch provides an in-document test guard and says evaluation should terminate when an operation is unsuccessful; an unsuccessful patch is not deemed successfully applied.
findings.notes: A revert payload can use an expected-preimage test as an additional stale-base check, provided the executor preserves all-or-none semantics.

findings.claim: HTTP If-Match uses strong entity-tag comparison before a state-changing method and can fail with 412 when the selected representation has changed, directly addressing lost updates.
findings.notes: The identity primitive is transferable to local file operations as a content or workspace hash plus a precondition check.

findings.claim: VS Code's agent-edit review keeps changes attributable and reversible at multiple granularities: individual inline edits, files, or all files, with explicit Keep/Undo and Discard actions and sensitive-file approval controls.
findings.notes: The product also warns that auto-accepted edits should be reviewed before source-control commit, making approval state part of safety.

findings.claim: VS Code separates request-level checkpoints from per-edit review: it snapshots affected files before a chat request, can restore all file changes after that point, can redo the restore, and can show per-request file change counts.
findings.notes: The documentation explicitly treats checkpoints as a batch/session aid that complements individual edit review.

findings.claim: VS Code local history is file-oriented: each save can create a full-content entry that supports compare and restore, including recovery of deleted files, while limits bound file size, entry count, exclusions, and merge windows.
findings.notes: This is distinct from Git commit history and from chat checkpoints because its unit is a saved file entry with configurable retention bounds.

findings.claim: No reviewed source defines a single cross-tool identity contract that binds agent task, request or turn, workspace snapshot, per-file preimage, postimage, actor, and rollback scope in one durable record.
findings.notes: This is a bounded absence finding from the 12 reviewed direct sources, not evidence that such a contract cannot be designed.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Use an explicit scope ladder: hunk or inline edit, file, selected path set, request checkpoint, then broader conversation or workspace rollback.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Puppet Master should make scope visible and require an explicit operation type for every level rather than treating file revert and turn rewind as aliases.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Preview before mutation with a diff or applicability check, then expose accept, reject, discard, or conflict outcomes.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A revert request should have a non-mutating preview that names paths, deletions, source revision, and expected result before commit.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Bind writes to an expected base using content identity and fail closed on a mismatch.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A local executor can use a strong preimage hash or blob identity and return a conflict that requires refresh or explicit force, rather than applying a stale revert.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Represent recoverable state as a named snapshot that can be inspected and reapplied, with conflicts preserving the recovery artifact.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Puppet Master should retain a pre-revert recovery capsule until post-apply validation succeeds, rather than deleting it at the first write.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: File-level review and turn-level checkpointing are complementary controls with different user intent and different affected-state boundaries.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: The product model should preserve the distinction in names, receipts, permissions, and recovery UX.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: No reviewed source documents a universal identity schema spanning IDE edits, Git state, agent requests, and conversation lineage.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Puppet Master must define this governance contract itself if cross-layer auditability is required; it should not assume an external convention exists.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A stale base or concurrent writer causes a patch or revert to apply against the wrong contents, producing a lost update or corruption.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Capture a strong preimage identity, check it immediately before mutation, and return a conflict or precondition failure without writing when it differs.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Direct in-place writes expose a partially written file or allow competing writers to interleave during revert.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Use exclusive intent, write to a same-filesystem temporary object, atomically publish, and define the multi-file transaction boundary; note that readers do not block on Git-style locks.

failure_modes.failure_mode: An overly broad or misbound restore silently removes tracked paths absent from the source or overwrites unrelated local edits.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Require explicit path selection, show deletion and overwrite counts in preview, and keep file-level revert separate from request or checkpoint rewind.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Reapplying a snapshot on a changed working state produces conflicts or an incomplete merge.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Preserve the snapshot on conflict, report affected paths and base identity, and require explicit conflict resolution or a new preview.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A local-history or checkpoint artifact expires, is size-limited, or excludes the target file, making an expected recovery unavailable.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Declare retention and durability in the operation contract; use a durable named snapshot for auditable recovery rather than relying only on bounded IDE history.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Automatic acceptance or source-control staging turns pending agent edits into accepted changes before a human or validator reviews them.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Make acceptance state explicit, preserve a diff, and require review or executable validation before durable commit.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A byte-atomic multi-file revert can still leave a semantically inconsistent project if related files are restored to mismatched revisions.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Treat atomic publication as necessary but insufficient; bind a source snapshot across the selected paths and run project-specific validation before closing the operation.

failure_modes.failure_mode: No reviewed source establishes a universal recovery journal that spans file state, agent request state, and conversation state with one identity and retention policy.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Define an explicit Puppet Master journal or document that the layers are intentionally independent; do not infer cross-layer rollback from a file snapshot.

implications.implication: A file-revert operation should name exact target paths, source snapshot or revision, destination layer, expected preimage identity, and preview result before any mutation.
implications.rationale: These sources consistently expose scope, source, diff or applicability, and review state as distinct controls.

implications.implication: The receipt should capture operation identity, actor or agent identity, request or attempt identity, worktree or workspace identity, selected paths, preimage and postimage hashes, source snapshot, outcome, and conflict reason.
implications.rationale: The sources provide separate examples of reference identity, snapshot identity, pending-edit attribution, and strong content preconditions; combining them is a Puppet Master design inference.

implications.implication: Apply only when the current base matches the captured identity; otherwise stop with a typed conflict and leave the target unchanged.
implications.rationale: Conditional PATCH, If-Match, and Git applicability checks all make stale-base rejection an explicit safety boundary.

implications.implication: Publish a successful revert atomically and retain the pre-revert recovery artifact until post-apply verification completes.
implications.rationale: Atomic publication protects visibility, while commit-backed stash behavior demonstrates why an inspectable recovery artifact should survive conflicts or uncertain outcomes.

implications.implication: Implement file revert and whole-turn or conversation rewind as separate operation types with separate confirmation, permissions, receipts, and recovery semantics.
implications.rationale: The reviewed IDE explicitly separates individual edit review from request checkpoints, while Git exposes path-scoped restore; the boundary is a direct product-design inference.

implications.implication: Use isolated worktree or workspace identities for agent attempts and previews when rollback must not disturb a user's active checkout.
implications.rationale: Git's linked worktree model shows a mature way to isolate HEAD and index state while sharing repository objects; applying it to agent attempts is an inferred Puppet Master pattern.

implications.implication: No reviewed source decides whether Puppet Master should rewind prompts or transcripts, so file-state recovery must not imply conversation-state mutation.
implications.rationale: The public sources document workspace and file rollback but do not define Puppet Master's desired transcript governance policy.

novel_ideas.idea: Add a Revert Preview Capsule that freezes the selected paths, source snapshot, base hashes, expected deletions, diffstat, conflict policy, and validation plan before execution.
novel_ideas.rationale: It combines Git's path and applicability controls with VS Code's visible review surface into one auditable pre-mutation object.

novel_ideas.idea: Use a two-tier Recoverability Envelope: short-lived request checkpoints for rapid experimentation and durable named content snapshots for file-level undo and audit.
novel_ideas.rationale: The sources show complementary transient IDE history and commit-backed Git recovery; separating their guarantees avoids promising IDE retention as durable governance evidence.

novel_ideas.idea: Record a monotonic revert journal with operation id, agent task id, request id, workspace or worktree id, preimage, postimage, atomic-commit marker, and validator result.
novel_ideas.rationale: This extends Git's commit and reference identity plus HTTP preconditions into a durable cross-layer receipt; the exact schema is not prescribed externally.

novel_ideas.idea: Represent rollback scope as a lattice from hunk to file to selected paths to request checkpoint to conversation, and reject an upward scope jump unless the user explicitly selects it.
novel_ideas.rationale: The lattice makes the scope difference visible and gives the executor a policy hook for preventing accidental whole-turn rewinds from a file-level command.

novel_ideas.idea: No reviewed tool document provides a standard API for proving that a revert did not alter excluded paths.
novel_ideas.rationale: Puppet Master could add an excluded-path hash set or workspace-wide before/after manifest as a novel integrity check, but its necessity and cost remain product decisions.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the authoritative revert source for untracked, ignored, newly created, or deleted files, and how is that source retained?
Which file metadata must participate in identity and rollback: symlink target, mode bits, submodule commit, encoding, permissions, and extended attributes?
What retention, durability, and garbage-collection guarantees distinguish a quick chat checkpoint from a governance-grade file recovery snapshot?
How should Puppet Master prove semantic validity after a byte-atomic multi-file revert, rather than treating atomic publication as sufficient?
Which immutable identity schema binds a file-revert operation to the agent task, turn or request, workspace or worktree, selected paths, and source snapshot?
Should whole-turn rewind alter conversation history, create a new branch of history, or preserve the transcript while changing only workspace state?
